name: Development
summary: One Go binary and PostgreSQL, one dependency, a documented REST API, modules compiled in, and an MCP server — with no cloud in the way.
title: Developer Experience — GoCommerce, Feature by Feature
description: GoCommerce for developers: one Go binary and PostgreSQL, one dependency, 342 documented REST operations, signed webhooks, an MCP server and agent guides.
ogTitle: Building on GoCommerce, feature by feature
ogDescription: One binary, one dependency, 342 documented operations, signed webhooks, MCP — and no cloud in the way.
h1: One binary, one database, one dependency
lede: GoCommerce is a Go program with its admin compiled in, talking to one PostgreSQL. Everything else — payments, carriers, search, an AI agent — is a module you import, and the whole API is written down in OpenAPI.

facts.t: modules, compiled in only when imported

tiles.title: One binary and PostgreSQL
tiles.text: The API and the 61-screen Svelte admin compile into one binary with go:embed. No Node.js at runtime, no cgo; it cross-compiles for Linux, Windows and macOS, and a distroless Docker image is provided.

tiles.title: One production dependency
tiles.text: go.mod requires only the pgx PostgreSQL driver, and modules add no third-party dependencies — CI enforces it.

tiles.title: Headless REST, documented
tiles.text: 342 operations — 238 in the core, the rest from modules — in OpenAPI 3.0.3, served at /doc and printed by gocommerce spec. The admin is itself a client of the same API.

tiles.title: MIT, all of it
tiles.text: The licence covers the whole repository. There is no closed or paid edition.

tiles.title: Modules, compiled in
tiles.text: 51 modules plug into a small set of ports; import one and it is in your binary. Narrower than a plugin store: modules are Go, compiled in, not installed at runtime.

tiles.title: Signed webhooks
tiles.text: The webhooks module posts signed events to any public https URL, with retries and a delivery log. Go code can also subscribe in-process.

tiles.title: Custom data
tiles.text: Fifteen core tables — products, variants, orders, carts, discounts, vendors and more — carry a free-form metadata object. Product attributes follow Shopify’s taxonomy, embedded in the binary, and can be filtered.

tiles.title: Admin screens from modules
tiles.text: A module adds an admin screen by describing a list and a form, gated by rights. Missing: shipping your own front-end code into the admin.

tiles.title: Any language
tiles.text: Anything that speaks JSON over HTTP can drive the API, and non-Go services receive events through signed webhooks.

tiles.title: gocommerce doctor
tiles.text: Nineteen health checks — the stock ledger, refunds, returns, event backlog, discounts, the API contract, sealed secrets — from the command line (non-zero exit on failure), the admin or the API.

tiles.title: Several instances, no coordination
tiles.text: Run more copies behind a load balancer: background work is claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and migrations run under an advisory lock. Uploads live on local disk, so instances share a volume for them.

tiles.title: Events that are never lost
tiles.text: Each event is written in the same transaction as the change it describes, delivered at least once with backoff, and parked after 12 failures on an Events screen where it can be retried.

tiles.title: Rate limits only at the doors
tiles.text: Operator sign-in, password reset and sign-up are throttled, and each AI agent key has its own number of requests a minute. Nothing else is limited: your server and database set the ceiling.

tiles.title: A command-line tool
tiles.text: serve, migrate, store, superuser, doctor, secrets, spec, taxonomy, attributes and version. Missing: environments, data branching and scaffolding.

tiles.title: Secrets sealed at rest
tiles.text: With GOCOMMERCE_SECRETS_KEY set, payment and provider keys, the copy of an API key and webhook signing secrets are stored sealed with AES-256-GCM, so a database dump holds ciphertext. gocommerce secrets seal seals what was stored before, and gocommerce doctor counts any left readable.

tiles.title: Addresses a store sets must be public
tiles.text: A webhook endpoint, a provider’s API base URL or a search host typed by a store is checked when saved and again at every connection, redirects included; private and loopback addresses are refused unless the install sets GOCOMMERCE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS, and doctor warns while it does.

tiles.title: No keys in the notification log
tiles.text: Reading the log of sent emails and SMS shows password-reset and invitation links, codes and tokens as “(hidden)”, for every reader, the owner included. The messages themselves are unchanged, and a resend still works.

tiles.title: A trace id on every request
tiles.text: Each request gets an id, returned in X-Trace-Id and printed on its log line beside the store; a caller may send its own. AI jobs, model runs and proposals keep the id of the request that caused them.

tiles.title: An MCP server
tiles.text: 19 tools that call the same domain services as the API — never the database — each checked against the caller’s rights. Read-only mode withholds every tool that changes anything, an agent key is offered the read tools only, and changes are logged. Over HTTP or stdio.

tiles.title: An AI gateway
tiles.text: Every model call a store makes goes through one module, which holds it to the store’s own key, a monthly cap and the kinds of data its owner lets out, and records what it cost.

tiles.title: Guides for coding agents
tiles.text: AGENTS.md sets 14 architectural rules and four notes for AI agents; skills/ holds 15 task guides and an index, so an agent reads the part of the domain it is about to change.

tiles.title: A test kit for module authors
tiles.text: gctest gives each test its own isolated database schema, and over a thousand tests catch a wrong edit.

notYetLede: Self-hosted, GoCommerce gives you standard PostgreSQL backups and point-in-time recovery rather than a hosted platform’s conveniences. Also absent today:

notYet.name: Sandboxes and data branching
notYet.why: No hosted environments; copy a store with pg_dump and pg_restore.

notYet.name: Managed backups and auto-scaling
notYet.why: Backups and scaling are yours, on your own infrastructure.

notYet.name: GraphQL
notYet.why: The API is REST and JSON.

notYet.name: Custom webhook payloads
notYet.why: Each event has a fixed body; you can filter events, not reshape them.

notYet.name: An app store
notYet.why: The Plugins screen configures modules already compiled in.

notYet.name: A generated client
notYet.why: Generate your own from the OpenAPI spec.

notYet.name: Data anonymisation
notYet.why: No tooling to mask production data.

faq.q: What do I need to run GoCommerce?
faq.a: One PostgreSQL database and somewhere to run one binary — a server, a container or your laptop. No Node.js, Redis or message broker is required.

Yes. Several instances can run behind a load balancer with no coordination between them; background work is claimed with row locks. Give them a shared volume for uploaded media, and size your PostgreSQL connection pooling.
No. The API is REST and JSON, documented in OpenAPI 3.0.3, so any language can generate a client from the spec.

faq.q: How do I add a feature the core does not have?
faq.a: Write a module: a Go package under ext/ that plugs into the core’s ports and is compiled in when imported. Or keep it outside GoCommerce entirely and listen to its signed webhooks.

faq.q: Can an AI agent run the store?
faq.a: Through the MCP module: 19 tools that go through the same services and rights checks as the API. Read-only mode lets an agent look without changing anything, and so does an agent key, which reaches the read tools only.
